properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-side client implementation of RFC 2617/7616 HTTP Digest auth used to exercise epee's RPC digest-auth server. MD5 is real here and mirrors the production digest algorithm in contrib/epee/src/http_auth.cpp (struct md5_ : digest_base_<EVP_md5,16>, "retained for backwards compatibility" per RFC 7616). Monero offers a disable_md5 flag in production; the test pins the legacy behaviour.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real but low-risk posture flag: the sampled sites compare PUBLIC values — levin protocol magic, boost archive signature, tx/block hash cache-integrity checks, cache tip hashes — where timing leakage reveals nothing secret; several other sites are functional-test asserts. The pattern is worth keeping on record because a few sites (updates.cpp hash check against signed update metadata) compare attacker-influenced data, and constant-time compare is cheap. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Trezor protocol session security: libsodium's crypto_aead_chacha20poly1305_ietf_decrypt authenticates/decrypts device session messages (protocol.cpp:127); the Poly1305 tag is the AEAD authenticator. ChaCha20-Poly1305 is PQ-robust (symmetric); the object survives on the confirmed decrypt site — the exception-class and throw sites were judged as non-operations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Wallet KDF posture: polyseed derives the wallet key from a 16-byte secret via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, but the iteration count is fixed inside the upstream polyseed library (polyseed.c), which is NOT vendored in this tree — only the wrapper (polyseed.cpp:88 injects crypto_pbkdf2_sha256) is. Upstream polyseed deliberately uses a low count (~10k, orders below OWASP's 600k) because the mnemonic itself carries ~128 bits of entropy, so the KDF is a stretching formality, not the sole barrier. Standardized

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: FCMP++ (full-chain membership proofs) Rust proving stack dependency: RustCrypto's k256 provides the secp256k1 group (ECDSA/sec-p256k1 arithmetic) used by the ciphersuite/curve-tree machinery that the daemon's fcmp_pp crate builds on. Dependency declaration inventory — presence is the fact; use is inside the vendored Rust build. Quantum-unsafe (Shor breaks secp256k1 discrete log).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: gen_ssl_cert is Monero's tool that generates a self-signed certificate and private key for daemon/wallet TLS; when a passphrase is given the PKCS#8 PEM is wrapped with OpenSSL's AES-128-CFB. CFB is malleable without authentication; the same file also uses SHA-256 to sign the cert. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two distinct ECDH surfaces: (1) epee's TLS cipher list pins ECDHE-ECDSA/RSA key exchange for daemon/wallet/P2P TLS — harvest-now-decrypt-later on all recorded Monero node traffic; (2) RingCT's ecdhEncode/ecdhDecode mask transaction amounts with ECDH-derived shared secrets on edwards25519 (device_default, device_ledger, Trezor protocol, multisig builder, rctSigs) — recorded chain traffic reveals amounts once ECDH falls. Migration needs a consensus-level hybrid KEM; not changeable locally.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Monero's signature machinery is ed25519-group based: the ref10 Ed25519 reference implementation is vendored in src/crypto/crypto_ops_builder (the harness that generated the shipped crypto-ops.c, with its /dev/urandom CSPRNG hook), and the FCMP++ Rust proving stack declares Ed25519 via ciphersuite and monero-oxide ec-divisors features. Shor breaks Ed25519 discrete log — the deadline (not harvest) PQ problem for the chain's signatures. The shipped crypto-ops.c ops (ring signatures, key images, der

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: These exports convert edwards25519 points (tx keys, output key derivations) into X25519 Montgomery u-coordinates — the key-agreement domain used for output derivation paths. X25519/ECDH is Shor-vulnerable (harvest-now-decrypt-later on recorded transaction derivations). Replaceable only by a chain-wide migration; not changeable locally without a hard fork.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: FCMP++ proving stack dependency: curve25519-dalek@4.1.3 supplies the Curve25519/Ed25519/Ristretto group arithmetic (dalek scalar/point types) used by the ciphersuite, ff/group and curve-tree machinery in the daemon's fcmp_pp crate. Quantum-unsafe: all recorded Curve25519 group operations fall to Shor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: FCMP++ proving stack dependency: RustCrypto's p256@0.13.2 provides the NIST P-256 (secp256r1) group and ECDSA, pulled in via the ciphersuite/ec-divisors crates of the daemon's fcmp_pp build. P-256 discrete log falls to Shor — quantum-unsafe signature/agreement primitive.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Monero's TLS 1.2 support is pinned by test: the shipped epee SSL layer (contrib/epee/src/net_ssl.cpp, other objects) serves TLS 1.2, so captured daemon/wallet/RPC P2P traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later material. Migration would be TLS 1.3 + hybrid X25519MLKEM768, which TLS 1.2 cannot negotiate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Monero's core hash and RNG: Keccak-256 (Keccak-f[1600], original 0x01 padding — cn_fast_hash) underpins tx/block hashing, ring signatures, key images, RingCT and multisig HMAC-Keccak. The same permutation is also Monero's userspace DRBG: src/crypto/random.c seeds an mlock'd Keccak sponge state from /dev/urandom (CryptGenRandom on Windows) and squeezes all secret material through generate_random_bytes_not_thread_safe / random_scalar (crypto.cpp:186) — a forward-secure SpongePRNG (keccak.team §4.3

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored BLAKE2b reference implementation (libsodium-style, with keyed/MAC parameter support) in src/crypto — shipped in the wallet/daemon libraries. BLAKE2 is unbroken and PQ-adequate for hashing; the interesting question (what Monero hashes with it) is answered by its callers in-tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 use sites: cert signing and fingerprinting in epee TLS (X509_sign/X509_digest, net_ssl.cpp:179/371), tools::sha256sum (src/common/util.cpp:689), HMAC-SHA256 core in polyseed's PBKDF2, and the SHA-256 variant of RFC 7616 digest auth exercised by the http unit tests. Strong digest; Grover gives only sqrt speedup — not urgent.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The PRF inside polyseed's PBKDF2 (see ALG-4de3b020): libsodium HMAC-SHA256 used as a KDF building block for deriving the polyseed wallet key. Strong, unbroken MAC; A- rating appropriate.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Polyseed mnemonic → wallet key derivation: the 16-byte polyseed secret is stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 via the injected callback. Wallet secret-key derivation from a user-memorized phrase — quantum-relevant only in that it wraps an ECC wallet key; PBKDF2 itself is the KDF. Changeable here in principle, but the polyseed format is cross-wallet standardized, so the parameters are fixed upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: FCMP++ proving stack dependency: RustCrypto's sha2@0.10.9 (SHA-256/SHA-512) — generic hash used by the ciphersuite/transcript machinery in the daemon's fcmp_pp crate. SHA-2 is PQ-adequate (Grover sqrt); inventory record, not urgent.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two distinct uses: (1) epee's pinned TLS cipher list admits ECDHE-AES256-GCM-SHA384 suites for daemon/wallet TLS — symmetric crypto is fine, the classical ECDHE key exchange in the same list is the PQ problem (covered by the ECDH object); (2) CryptoNight PoW uses AES-256 rounds — a hash workload, not data protection. AES-256 survives Grover with margin.
